newsitem.title: UK: European aluminium premiums may firm in near term.
newsitem.headline: European aluminium premiums may firm in near term.

text.p: Premiums in the European physical aluminium market remained firm on Tuesday and may well push higher in the short-term due to a dearth of Russian availability, traders said.
"Premiums and demand are quite steady and CIS (metal) is very tight in Europe because it is all going to the U.S.," one said.
Some said that premiums were steady but as there had been little movement, would-be sellers may have to lower their asking ideas.
But others traders reported recent business for Russian A7E aluminium at a premium of $38, while Western ingots have traded at $48 -- in both cases the higher end of quotes.
Although the overall level of business this month has been down on Jan/Feb, there was covering that needed to be done for the start of the second quarter.

Because there was little Russian aluminium around -- some traders said that up to 50,000 tonnes had moved across the Atlantic to feed high spot-Midwest premiums -- European premiums could spike upwards by about $10 next month.
